theme: Typefaces with serifs: small finishing strokes project from the ends of the main strokes of each letter.
decoy: Classic typefaces with long print histories

members.title: Garamond
members.description: Sixteenth-century French roman revived countless times for book text.

members.title: Baskerville
members.description: High-contrast 1750s English face cut for a Birmingham printer and japanner.

members.title: Bodoni
members.description: Stark Italian face with hairline contrast, favored by fashion magazines.

members.title: Caslon
members.description: Eighteenth-century English face used to print the Declaration of Independence.

members.title: Didot
members.description: Parisian high-contrast face from around 1800, a masthead staple.

members.title: Palatino
members.description: Hermann Zapf's calligraphic face drawn after Italian Renaissance writing masters.

members.title: Clarendon
members.description: Sturdy 1845 English display face seen on Victorian posters.

members.title: Rockwell
members.description: Geometric 1934 Monotype display face with an even, heavy weight.

members.title: Trajan
members.description: Carol Twombly's all-capital face based on an inscription at a Roman column's base.

intruders.title: Optima
intruders.description: Hermann Zapf's elegant roman with gently swelling, tapered verticals.
intruders.why: A humanist sans-serif: its strokes flare toward the ends but carry no serifs. Its classical proportions and designer make it read like a book face.

intruders.title: Lithos
intruders.description: Carol Twombly's all-capital display face based on ancient Greek inscriptions.
intruders.why: A sans-serif. Like Twombly's Trajan it revives ancient carved capitals, but its Greek letterforms have no serifs.

theme: Monospaced typefaces, in which every glyph occupies the same horizontal width.
decoy: Typefaces with a typewriter or computer-terminal flavor

members.title: Courier
members.description: Slab face drawn by Howard Kettler for IBM typewriters in 1955.

members.title: Consolas
members.description: Microsoft face bundled with Windows Vista and Visual Studio.

members.title: Lucida Console
members.description: Sans face from the Lucida family long offered in Windows command windows.

members.title: Menlo
members.description: Apple's 2009 face derived from Bitstream Vera, used in Xcode.

members.title: Inconsolata
members.description: Open-source face by Raph Levien, inspired by Consolas.

members.title: OCR-A
members.description: Blocky 1968 face designed for machine reading on checks and forms.

members.title: Letter Gothic
members.description: Clean sans face drawn by Roger Roberson for IBM typewriters.

members.title: Monaco
members.description: Compact sans face shipped on Macs since the 1980s, a programmer favorite.

intruders.title: American Typewriter
intruders.description: Rounded slab face from 1974 evoking office-machine output.
intruders.why: Proportionally spaced: Joel Kaden and Tony Stan drew it to look typewritten while letting narrow letters take less room.

intruders.title: Lucida Grande
intruders.description: Humanist sans face from the Lucida family used for Mac OS X menus.
intruders.why: A proportional face. It shares the Lucida family with Lucida Console, but its letters vary in width.

theme: Logos whose emblem depicts a real animal species rather than a mythical creature.
decoy: Brand logos built around a creature

members.title: Ferrari
members.description: Black prancing horse on a yellow shield, from Maranello.

members.title: Lamborghini
members.description: Gold charging bull on the black shield of an Italian supercar maker.

members.title: Peugeot
members.description: Lion rearing on its hind legs, on French car badges.

members.title: Lacoste
members.description: Small green crocodile stitched onto the chest of a piqué polo.

members.title: Twitter
members.description: Small blue bird in flight, used by a microblogging service.

members.title: MGM
members.description: Roaring lion framed by a film-strip ring before studio features.

members.title: Bacardi
members.description: Black bat with outstretched wings on a rum bottle label.

members.title: Abarth
members.description: Scorpion on a red and yellow shield, on tuned Italian small cars.

intruders.title: Mobil
intruders.description: Red winged horse on the signage of a petroleum brand.
intruders.why: Pegasus is a creature of Greek myth. It looks like a cousin of Ferrari's horse, but no real species has wings.

intruders.title: Vauxhall
intruders.description: Griffin on the grilles and badges of a British carmaker.
intruders.why: The griffin is a mythical lion-eagle hybrid, not a real animal, though it sits on car badges like Peugeot's lion.

theme: Hats with a brim that runs all the way around the crown.
decoy: Classic men's hats

members.title: Fedora
members.description: Soft felt hat with a lengthwise dent and a pinched front.

members.title: Trilby
members.description: Narrow felt hat angled down at the back, often worn tipped forward.

members.title: Bowler
members.description: Hard, rounded felt hat of London clerks and Charlie Chaplin.

members.title: Panama hat
members.description: Pale hat woven from toquilla straw in Ecuador.

members.title: Boater
members.description: Stiff flat-topped straw hat with a ribbon band, for summer regattas.

members.title: Pork pie hat
members.description: Flat-topped felt hat with a circular groove, linked to jazz musicians.

members.title: Homburg
members.description: Stiff felt hat with a single center dent and a bound edge.

members.title: Top hat
members.description: Tall silk-plush cylinder for formal evening and daytime dress.

intruders.title: Deerstalker
intruders.description: Tweed hat with ear flaps tied on top, linked to Sherlock Holmes.
intruders.why: It has two peaks, one at the front and one at the back, and nothing at the sides. It is still a classic menswear hat with projecting shade.

intruders.title: Flat cap
intruders.description: Rounded tweed hat with a small stiff peak, worn in the countryside.
intruders.why: Its short peak projects only at the front, like a visor.

theme: Devices that play back recorded audio (tapes, discs, vinyl, or stored files) rather than only receiving broadcasts.
decoy: Iconic portable and home audio gadgets

members.title: Sony Walkman TPS-L2
members.description: Blue-and-silver 1979 portable with two headphone jacks and a hotline button.

members.title: Sony Discman D-50
members.description: Sony's squat, square 1984 portable with a flip-up lid.

members.title: iPod (first generation)
members.description: White 2001 pocket gadget with a mechanical scroll wheel and a hard drive.

members.title: iPod shuffle
members.description: Tiny screenless clip-on gadget that can mix up song order.

members.title: Zune
members.description: Microsoft's 2006 portable, offered in brown, with wireless song sharing.

members.title: Diamond Rio PMP300
members.description: 1998 pocket MP3 gadget that the music industry sued to stop.

members.title: Dansette
members.description: Two-tone British portable turntable cabinet of 1950s teenage bedrooms.

members.title: Victrola
members.description: Wooden cabinet phonograph with its horn hidden behind doors.

intruders.title: Braun T3
intruders.description: Dieter Rams' 1958 pocket gadget with a perforated grille and a round dial.
intruders.why: A radio receiver only: it tunes stations and cannot play any recording. Its dial-and-grille face famously prefigured the iPod.

intruders.title: Brionvega TS 502
intruders.description: Hinged red cube that opens to reveal a speaker and tuning dials.
intruders.why: An AM/FM radio only, with no mechanism for recordings.

intruders.title: Regency TR-1
intruders.description: 1954 pocket gadget sold in brightly colored plastic cases.
intruders.why: The first commercial transistor radio: it only receives stations, though it was the Walkman of its day.

theme: Timepieces that show the time as numerals on a digital readout, with no hands.
decoy: Iconic watches and clocks of the late 20th century

members.title: Hamilton Pulsar P1
members.description: 1972 gold-cased wrist computer that lights up red at a button press.

members.title: Casio F-91W
members.description: Cheap black resin 1989 Casio with a tiny backlight and an alarm.

members.title: Casio G-Shock DW-5000C
members.description: 1983 resin watch engineered to survive a ten-meter drop.

members.title: Casio CA-53W
members.description: Slim Casio wrist calculator with a tiny rubber keypad.

members.title: Timex Ironman
members.description: 1986 triathlon sports watch with a lap-counting stopwatch.

members.title: Timex Datalink
members.description: 1994 Timex that synced data from flashing lines on a PC monitor.

members.title: Seiko 06LC
members.description: 1973 Seiko quartz watch with a six-figure liquid-crystal panel.

members.title: Solari Cifra 3
members.description: Gino Valle's 1965 cylindrical table clock with flipping plastic leaves.

intruders.title: Casio MQ-24
intruders.description: Cheap black resin Casio with a plain white face and a buckle strap.
intruders.why: An analog quartz watch with hands. It is as cheap and ubiquitous as the F-91W.

intruders.title: Swatch
intruders.description: 1983 Swiss plastic quartz watch with a sealed, welded case.
intruders.why: The original Swatch tells time with hands, though it shares the Casios' plastic, quartz and mass-market appeal.

intruders.title: Nelson Ball Clock
intruders.description: George Nelson's 1949 wall clock ringed by twelve wooden balls.
intruders.why: It tells time with hands; the balls only mark the hours. Like the Cifra 3, it is a design-classic clock.

theme: Devices with a built-in physical keyboard for typing text.
decoy: Landmark typewriters, computers and handheld gadgets

members.title: Olivetti Valentine
members.description: Ettore Sottsass's red plastic portable with a matching carry case, 1969.

members.title: IBM Selectric
members.description: 1961 office machine with a spinning golf-ball type element.

members.title: IBM Model M
members.description: Heavy 1985 buckling-spring peripheral, famous for its clatter.

members.title: Commodore 64
members.description: 1982 beige home computer housing all its circuitry in one wedge.

members.title: ZX Spectrum
members.description: Sinclair's 1982 black home computer with rubbery rainbow-striped styling.

members.title: Nokia 9000 Communicator
members.description: 1996 clamshell phone that opens to reveal a small office computer.

members.title: Psion Series 5
members.description: 1997 pocket organizer whose lid slides forward as it opens.

members.title: BlackBerry Bold
members.description: Glossy 2008 smartphone with a leather-textured back and a trackball.

members.title: TRS-80 Model 100
members.description: Battery-powered 1983 portable computer with a wide monochrome LCD strip.

intruders.title: PalmPilot
intruders.description: 1996 pocket organizer with a monochrome screen and a slot-in stylus.
intruders.why: Input is Graffiti handwriting with a stylus; there is no built-in keyboard. It competed directly with Psion's organizers.

intruders.title: Apple Newton MessagePad
intruders.description: Apple's 1993 handheld organizer with a large gray screen and stylus.
intruders.why: It relied on handwriting recognition; keyboards were only optional external accessories.

theme: Pendant lights: fixtures that hang suspended from the ceiling.
decoy: Famous modern lamps

members.title: PH5
members.description: Poul Henningsen's 1958 lamp of stacked curved shades that hide the bulb.

members.title: PH Artichoke
members.description: Copper leaves in staggered rows around a bulb, first made for a Copenhagen restaurant.

members.title: Taraxacum
members.description: Castiglioni brothers' cocoon of sprayed resin over a steel skeleton.

members.title: Heracleum
members.description: Bertjan Pot's branching metal stems ending in small LED lenses.

members.title: Flowerpot VP1
members.description: Verner Panton's 1968 lamp of two stacked enameled hemispheres.

members.title: Frisbi
members.description: Achille Castiglioni's translucent disc floating below a small metal shade.

members.title: Zettel'z
members.description: Ingo Maurer's lamp bristling with clipped paper notes on wires.

members.title: Le Klint 101
members.description: Hand-pleated shade folded in Denmark from a single sheet.

intruders.title: Arco
intruders.description: Castiglioni brothers' arching steel stem rising from a heavy marble block.
intruders.why: A floor lamp: the arc carries the shade over a table to mimic a pendant without ceiling wiring.

intruders.title: Twiggy
intruders.description: Marc Sadler's slender fiberglass arc bending over to hold a shade aloft.
intruders.why: A floor lamp whose flexible arc places the shade overhead; nothing is attached to the ceiling.

theme: Chairs whose frame, legs included, is made of wood rather than metal.
decoy: Classic dining and lounge chairs

members.title: Thonet No. 14
members.description: Six steam-bent parts and ten screws, shipped flat-packed from 1859.

members.title: Wishbone Chair
members.description: Hans Wegner's Y-backed design with a hand-woven paper-cord seat.

members.title: Windsor chair
members.description: English country seat with turned spindles socketed into a carved saddle.

members.title: Red and Blue Chair
members.description: Rietveld's angular De Stijl seat of primary-colored planes and black battens.

members.title: Paimio Chair
members.description: Alvar Aalto's sanatorium armchair with a scrolled bent-plywood seat.

members.title: Peacock Chair
members.description: Hans Wegner's armchair with a fan of flattened spindles behind the sitter.

members.title: Shaker ladder-back chair
members.description: Plain side chair with horizontal slats and a woven seat, from a religious community.

members.title: Adirondack chair
members.description: Slatted outdoor lounger with a sloped seat and broad flat armrests.

intruders.title: Ant Chair
intruders.description: Arne Jacobsen's pinch-waisted plywood chair, first made with three supports.
intruders.why: Its legs are chromed tubular steel; only the seat shell is plywood.

intruders.title: Series 7
intruders.description: Arne Jacobsen's hourglass plywood chair, stacked in countless cafes.
intruders.why: The plywood shell sits on tubular steel legs.

intruders.title: Eames Lounge Chair
intruders.description: Molded rosewood plywood shells with leather cushions and a matching ottoman.
intruders.why: The plywood shells ride on a cast-aluminum swivel base joined by aluminum braces.

theme: Cantilever chairs, which stand on a single continuous support with no rear legs.
decoy: Modernist chairs of bent tube, plywood or plastic

members.title: Cesca Chair
members.description: Marcel Breuer's chrome tubular steel design with a caned seat and back.

members.title: MR10 Chair
members.description: Mies van der Rohe's sweeping chrome tube design shown in Stuttgart in 1927.

members.title: S33 Chair
members.description: Mart Stam's chrome tube design, inspired by gas pipes, with a leather seat.

members.title: Brno Chair
members.description: Mies van der Rohe's flat steel bar armchair for the Tugendhat villa.

members.title: Zig-Zag Chair
members.description: Gerrit Rietveld's four wooden planks joined in a Z silhouette.

members.title: S-Chair
members.description: Tom Dixon's sinuous rush-woven design on a welded steel skeleton.

members.title: Armchair 406
members.description: Alvar Aalto's birch armchair with fabric webbing stretched between bent runners.

members.title: B35 Lounge Chair
members.description: Marcel Breuer's chrome tube lounge armchair with wooden armrests.

intruders.title: Wassily Chair
intruders.description: Marcel Breuer's chrome tube armchair with taut leather straps.
intruders.why: Its tubular frame meets the floor on runners at both front and back, so nothing is cantilevered. It shares the Cesca's designer and material.

intruders.title: Barcelona Chair
intruders.description: Mies van der Rohe's X-framed steel lounge chair with tufted leather cushions.
intruders.why: Its crossed steel legs support the seat at front and back; it has no cantilever, unlike Mies's MR10.

theme: Chairs molded as one single piece of material, with no separate base, legs, or fasteners.
decoy: Sculptural modern plastic chairs

members.title: Panton Chair
members.description: Verner Panton's flowing S-curve plastic chair, a glossy icon of 1960s pop.

members.title: Air-Chair
members.description: Jasper Morrison's stackable polypropylene chair made by gas-assisted injection.

members.title: Selene
members.description: Vico Magistretti's 1969 fiberglass chair with S-profiled supports.

members.title: Bofinger Chair
members.description: Helmut Bätzner's 1966 stackable fiberglass-polyester chair from a German firm.

members.title: Bellini Chair
members.description: Mario Bellini's 1998 stackable polypropylene chair for Heller.

members.title: White resin patio chair
members.description: Cheap stackable garden chair found on terraces worldwide.

members.title: Tip Ton
members.description: Barber Osgerby's polypropylene chair that tilts forward on its skids.

members.title: Myto
members.description: Konstantin Grcic's perforated plastic cantilever chair released in 2008.

intruders.title: Tulip Chair
intruders.description: Eero Saarinen's white chair that seems to grow from a single stem.
intruders.why: The fiberglass shell sits on a separate cast-aluminum base. Saarinen wanted one material but could not achieve it, so it only looks monolithic.

intruders.title: Eames Plastic Side Chair
intruders.description: Charles and Ray Eames's 1950 fiberglass shell chair in soft muted colors.
intruders.why: The shell is bolted, via rubber shock mounts, to separate wire or wooden bases.

intruders.title: Tom Vac
intruders.description: Ron Arad's rippled polypropylene chair, first made in aluminum in Milan.
intruders.why: The rippled shell is fixed onto separate tubular steel legs.

theme: Cars whose engine sits at the rear, behind the passenger compartment.
decoy: Iconic small and sporty cars of the 20th century

members.title: Volkswagen Beetle
members.description: Rounded German economy car built for decades with minimal change.

members.title: Porsche 911
members.description: Sloping-fastback German sports coupe first shown in 1963.

members.title: Fiat Nuova 500
members.description: Tiny 1957 Italian city car with a roll-back fabric roof.

members.title: Renault 4CV
members.description: Small postwar French four-door nicknamed the 'motte de beurre'.

members.title: Tatra T87
members.description: Streamlined 1930s Czech sedan with a tall dorsal fin.

members.title: DeLorean DMC-12
members.description: Brushed stainless-steel gull-winged coupe built in Northern Ireland.

members.title: Chevrolet Corvair
members.description: Compact 1960s American car attacked in 'Unsafe at Any Speed'.

members.title: Volkswagen Type 2
members.description: Split-windshield German van beloved by surfers and campers.

members.title: Smart Fortwo
members.description: Two-seat microcar short enough to park nose-in to the curb.

intruders.title: Mini
intruders.description: Tiny 1959 British two-door with its wheels pushed to the corners.
intruders.why: Its engine sits transversely at the front, driving the front wheels. It shares the Fiat 500's small-car fame.

intruders.title: Citroën 2CV
intruders.description: Corrugated French economy car with a roll-back canvas roof.
intruders.why: Its flat-twin engine is at the front, driving the front wheels. Its canvas roof and mission echo the Fiat 500 and Beetle.

intruders.title: Trabant
intruders.description: East German economy car with a plastic body reinforced by cotton.
intruders.why: Its two-stroke engine is at the front, driving the front wheels, though it was the Eastern bloc's people's car like the Beetle.

theme: Clothing and eyewear first developed for military use before becoming civilian fashion.
decoy: Classic menswear staples with utilitarian origins

members.title: Trench coat
members.description: Belted double-breasted gabardine coat with epaulettes and a storm flap.

members.title: MA-1 bomber jacket
members.description: Nylon jacket with a knit collar and a bright orange lining.

members.title: Peacoat
members.description: Short dark wool coat with broad lapels and large buttons.

members.title: Cargo pants
members.description: Loose trousers with large bellows pockets on the thighs.

members.title: Ray-Ban Aviator
members.description: Teardrop-lensed metal-framed sunglasses with a double bridge.

members.title: M-65 jacket
members.description: Olive cotton-nylon jacket with four front pockets and a hood stowed in the collar.

members.title: Chinos
members.description: Lightweight cotton twill trousers in shades of khaki and stone.

members.title: Fishtail parka
members.description: Hooded olive parka with a split tail, adopted by 1960s mods.

intruders.title: Clarks Desert Boot
intruders.description: Lightweight suede ankle boot on a crepe sole, worn by 1960s mods.
intruders.why: Nathan Clark designed it for civilian sale, inspired by boots officers had made in Cairo bazaars. The military link is inspiration, not issue.

intruders.title: Levi's 501
intruders.description: Riveted indigo denim trousers with a button fly and leather patch.
intruders.why: Made as workwear for miners and laborers, not for soldiers.

theme: Products designed or co-designed by Dieter Rams.
decoy: Modernist Braun and Vitsoe products of the 1950s to 1980s

members.title: Braun SK 4
members.description: 1956 radio-phonograph with a clear acrylic lid, nicknamed Snow White's Coffin.

members.title: Vitsoe 606 Universal Shelving System
members.description: Wall-mounted aluminum track shelving launched in 1960.

members.title: Vitsoe 620 Chair Programme
members.description: Modular 1962 lounge seating on a swivel or fixed base.

members.title: Braun T 1000
members.description: Aluminum-cased 1963 multiband world receiver built for globe-trotting listeners.

members.title: Braun ET 66
members.description: 1987 black pocket calculator with convex round buttons.

members.title: Braun TP 1
members.description: 1959 portable pairing a pocket receiver with a small phonograph.

members.title: Braun T 2 lighter
members.description: Cylindrical 1968 table lighter in chrome or black.

members.title: Braun HLD 4
members.description: Compact 1970 handheld hair dryer with a slim angular body.

intruders.title: Braun Sixtant
intruders.description: 1962 electric shaver in black with a matte silver foil head.
intruders.why: Designed by Hans Gugelot and Gerd Alfred Müller. It is a quintessential Braun object of the Rams era, but not his work.

intruders.title: Braun KF 20
intruders.description: Cylindrical 1972 drip coffee maker in tiers of colored plastic.
intruders.why: Designed by Florian Seiffert, a member of the Braun team Rams led.

theme: Typefaces created on commission for one organization's own use, such as a newspaper, transit network, road authority or company.
decoy: Influential twentieth-century typefaces

members.title: Johnston
members.description: Edward Johnston's 1916 humanist sans with diamond-shaped dots on i and j.

members.title: Times New Roman
members.description: Stanley Morison's compact 1932 roman for narrow columns.

members.title: Transport
members.description: Kinneir and Calvert's mixed-case sans for British motorway signs.

members.title: Frutiger
members.description: Adrian Frutiger's open humanist sans, first seen on Paris airport signs.

members.title: Verdana
members.description: Matthew Carter's wide sans tuned for low-resolution screens.

members.title: Bell Centennial
members.description: Matthew Carter's sans with ink traps for tiny phone-directory listings.

members.title: Rail Alphabet
members.description: Crisp sans seen on British station signage from 1965.

members.title: Calvert
members.description: Margaret Calvert's slab serif for the signs of a Tyneside metro.

members.title: Highway Gothic
members.description: Condensed American sans family lettered on interstate signs.

intruders.title: Univers
intruders.description: Adrian Frutiger's 1957 sans issued in a numbered grid of 21 styles.
intruders.why: Released commercially by the Deberny & Peignot foundry, not made for a client. Frutiger's later airport face was the commissioned one.

intruders.title: Futura
intruders.description: Paul Renner's geometric 1927 sans that went to the Moon on a plaque.
intruders.why: A commercial release from the Bauer Type Foundry; its famous uses came later and were not commissions.

theme: Design objects created by Finnish designers.
decoy: Nordic modern design classics

members.title: Savoy vase
members.description: Alvar Aalto's wavy-walled glass vase from 1936.

members.title: Ball Chair
members.description: Eero Aarnio's fiberglass globe seat with a padded interior, 1963.

members.title: Teema
members.description: Kaj Franck's plain tableware built on circles, squares and rectangles.

members.title: Stool 60
members.description: Alvar Aalto's stackable three-legged wooden stool with L-shaped birch legs.

members.title: Birds by Toikka
members.description: Oiva Toikka's hand-blown glass birds, each slightly different.

members.title: Kivi votive
members.description: Heikki Orvola's thick glass tealight holder made in dozens of colors.

members.title: Aarne glassware
members.description: Göran Hongell's heavy-based drinking glasses from 1948.

members.title: Jokapoika shirt
members.description: Vuokko Nurmesniemi's striped cotton shirt for Marimekko, 1956.

intruders.title: Kay Bojesen monkey
intruders.description: Kay Bojesen's jointed wooden monkey toy of teak and limba.
intruders.why: Bojesen was Danish. His toy sits naturally beside Toikka's birds as a Nordic collectible.

intruders.title: IKEA Poäng
intruders.description: Noboru Nakamura's bentwood armchair for a flat-pack retailer.
intruders.why: Designed by a Japanese designer for Swedish IKEA; its bent birch recalls Aalto's work.

theme: Wristwatches designed for underwater diving.
decoy: Classic mid-century steel tool watches

members.title: Rolex Submariner
members.description: 1953 steel watch with a black bezel and Mercedes-style hands.

members.title: Blancpain Fifty Fathoms
members.description: 1953 steel watch with a broad black bezel and luminous markers.

members.title: Omega Seamaster 300
members.description: 1957 steel watch with broad-arrow hands and a black bezel.

members.title: Seiko SKX007
members.description: Affordable Japanese automatic with its crown at four o'clock.

members.title: Doxa Sub 300
members.description: 1967 Swiss watch with a bright orange dial and a cushion case.

members.title: Panerai Radiomir
members.description: Oversized cushion-cased Italian watch with radium-paint numerals.

members.title: Rolex Sea-Dweller
members.description: Thick-cased 1967 steel watch with a black bezel and a date.

members.title: Omega Ploprof
members.description: Chunky 1970 steel watch with a monobloc case and a red bezel-lock button.

intruders.title: Rolex GMT-Master
intruders.description: 1954 steel watch with a two-tone red and blue rotating bezel.
intruders.why: Developed with Pan Am for airline pilots tracking two time zones. It shares the Submariner's case and rotating bezel.

intruders.title: Omega Speedmaster Professional
intruders.description: 1957 steel chronograph with a tachymeter scale, worn on the Moon.
intruders.why: A racing chronograph later flown by NASA; it was never built for use in water.

intruders.title: Rolex Explorer
intruders.description: 1953 steel watch with a black dial and bold 3-6-9 numerals.
intruders.why: Tied to mountaineering and the 1953 Everest expedition, not to the sea.

theme: Sneakers originally designed as basketball shoes.
decoy: Classic sneakers that crossed over into streetwear

members.title: Converse Chuck Taylor All Star
members.description: Canvas high-top with a rubber toe cap and an ankle patch.

members.title: Nike Air Jordan 1
members.description: 1985 leather high-top in red, black and white with a winged logo.

members.title: Nike Blazer
members.description: Early-1970s leather or suede high-top with an oversized side logo.

members.title: Adidas Superstar
members.description: White leather low-top with a ridged rubber shell toe.

members.title: Puma Clyde
members.description: Suede low-top with a contrasting side stripe, a 1970s New York favorite.

members.title: Nike Dunk
members.description: 1985 leather model issued in bold two-tone colorways.

members.title: Reebok Pump
members.description: 1989 high-top with an inflatable tongue and a pump button.

members.title: Nike Air Force 1
members.description: 1982 all-white leather model with a chunky cupsole.

intruders.title: Adidas Stan Smith
intruders.description: White leather low-top with perforated stripes and green heel tab.
intruders.why: A tennis shoe, first sold as the Robert Haillet. Its clean white leather makes it look like the Superstar.

intruders.title: Adidas Samba
intruders.description: Slim low-top with a gum sole and a suede T-shaped toe overlay.
intruders.why: Made for football training on frozen ground, not basketball.

intruders.title: Nike Air Max 1
intruders.description: 1987 low-top with a visible heel air unit and mesh panels.
intruders.why: A running shoe, though it sits alongside the Air Force 1 and Jordan 1 in sneaker culture.

theme: Apple products designed by the industrial design group Jony Ive led (1996-2019).
decoy: Landmark Apple hardware

members.title: iMac G3
members.description: Egg-shaped all-in-one computer in translucent Bondi Blue plastic.

members.title: Power Mac G4 Cube
members.description: Eight-inch clear acrylic cube with a slot-loading optical drive on top.

members.title: iMac G4
members.description: White dome base with a flat screen on a chrome swiveling arm.

members.title: iPhone
members.description: Glass-fronted touchscreen phone with a single round home button.

members.title: MacBook Air
members.description: Wedge-shaped aluminum laptop pulled from a manila envelope on stage.

members.title: iPad
members.description: Thin aluminum-backed touchscreen slate with a single round home button.

members.title: Apple Watch
members.description: Rounded rectangular wrist computer with a digital crown.

members.title: AirPods
members.description: White wireless earbuds with stems, stored in a flip-top charging case.

intruders.title: Macintosh 128K
intruders.description: Apple's beige all-in-one with a built-in nine-inch screen and handle.
intruders.why: Designed by Jerry Manock and Terry Oyama's team, years before Ive joined Apple.

intruders.title: Apple IIc
intruders.description: Apple's compact off-white portable computer with a fold-down handle.
intruders.why: Designed with Hartmut Esslinger's frogdesign in the 'Snow White' language, long before Ive's group.

theme: Logos that hide a figure formed by negative space, the empty area between or around the drawn shapes.
decoy: Famous logos with a hidden image or message

members.title: FedEx
members.description: Purple and orange wordmark of an overnight courier.

members.title: Toblerone
members.description: Matterhorn silhouette on the box of a triangular Swiss chocolate bar.

members.title: Carrefour
members.description: Red and blue arrow-like wedges for a French hypermarket chain.

members.title: Pittsburgh Zoo & PPG Aquarium
members.description: Stylized black tree above the name of a Pennsylvania zoo.

members.title: Guild of Food Writers
members.description: Fountain-pen nib emblem of a British association of cookery authors.

members.title: NBC
members.description: Six colored feathers fanning out, for an American TV network.

members.title: Formula 1 (1994-2017)
members.description: Black slanted F beside red speed stripes, for motor racing's top series.

members.title: Hartford Whalers
members.description: Green W topped by a blue whale's tail, for a hockey team.

intruders.title: Tostitos
intruders.description: Bold wordmark of an American tortilla-chip and salsa brand.
intruders.why: Its two t's are drawn as people sharing a chip over a salsa-bowl i-dot. The hidden picture comes from the letters themselves, not from negative space.

intruders.title: Tour de France
intruders.description: Hand-lettered wordmark of cycling's most famous three-week race.
intruders.why: Its hidden cyclist is drawn by the letter R with a round yellow wheel, which are positive shapes, not empty space.

theme: Brand names taken from genuine words or phrases in a language other than English.
decoy: Brands with foreign-sounding names

members.title: Audi
members.description: German carmaker whose badge is four interlocking silver rings.

members.title: Volvo
members.description: Swedish carmaker known for boxy estates and safety engineering.

members.title: Vespa
members.description: Italian step-through scooter with a pressed-steel body.

members.title: Nivea
members.description: German skin cream sold in a flat blue tin with white lettering.

members.title: Hyundai
members.description: South Korean carmaker behind the Pony, its first home-grown model.

members.title: Samsung
members.description: South Korean electronics giant behind the Galaxy phones.

members.title: Le Creuset
members.description: French maker of enameled cast-iron pots in graded orange.

members.title: Fjällräven
members.description: Swedish outdoor label behind the boxy Kånken backpack.

intruders.title: Häagen-Dazs
intruders.description: American ice cream brand sold in small round pint cartons.
intruders.why: The name is invented gibberish styled to sound Danish; it is not a word in any language.

intruders.title: Rolex
intruders.description: Swiss watchmaker whose crown logo tops the Oyster case.
intruders.why: Hans Wilsdorf coined the name; despite its Latin ring it is not a word in any language.

theme: Typefaces named after a city.
decoy: Typefaces with place-name titles

members.title: Chicago
members.description: Heavy bitmap sans that labeled the menus of the original Macintosh.

members.title: Geneva
members.description: Neat bitmap sans for small interface text, modeled on a Swiss grotesque.

members.title: London
members.description: Bitmap blackletter face in the Old English manner.

members.title: Venice
members.description: Bill Atkinson's slanted calligraphic bitmap script.

members.title: San Francisco
members.description: Ransom-note bitmap face whose letters look cut from newspapers.

members.title: Cairo
members.description: Bitmap font of tiny pictograms, home of Clarus the dogcow.

members.title: Memphis
members.description: Rudolf Wolf's geometric slab serif, released by Stempel in 1929.

members.title: Zurich
members.description: Bitstream's version of Univers, sold under a different trade title.

intruders.title: Helvetica
intruders.description: Max Miedinger's neutral 1957 grotesque from the Haas foundry.
intruders.why: Its name is Latin for 'Swiss', a country rather than a city. Geneva was drawn after it.

intruders.title: Georgia
intruders.description: Matthew Carter's screen serif for Microsoft with old-style numerals.
intruders.why: Named after a tabloid headline about alien heads found in Georgia, a US state rather than a city.

theme: Brand names that a court or trademark office formally ruled to be generic words, ending the owner's exclusive claim to them in that country.
decoy: Everyday products known by a brand-like coinage

members.title: Escalator
members.description: Moving staircase of linked steps, promoted by Otis from 1900.

members.title: Thermos
members.description: Vacuum-insulated bottle keeping drinks hot or cold for hours.

members.title: Yo-yo
members.description: Spool that climbs back up its string when flicked, sold by Duncan.

members.title: Cellophane
members.description: Transparent film of regenerated cellulose, sold by DuPont for wrapping.

members.title: Aspirin
members.description: Pain-relief tablet of acetylsalicylic acid, first sold by Bayer.

members.title: Linoleum
members.description: Floor covering of linseed oil and cork on a canvas backing.

members.title: Shredded Wheat
members.description: Pillow-shaped biscuits of baked wheat strands, eaten with milk.

members.title: Murphy bed
members.description: Bed that pivots up on a hinge into a wall cabinet.

intruders.title: Nylon
intruders.description: Synthetic polyamide fiber from DuPont that replaced silk in stockings.
intruders.why: DuPont deliberately never registered 'nylon' as a trademark, so no ruling was ever needed; it is a coinage people widely assume was a lost brand name.

intruders.title: Spandex
intruders.description: Stretchy polyurethane fiber from DuPont used in leggings and cycling shorts.
intruders.why: Coined as the generic fiber name (an anagram of 'expands'); DuPont's brand was Lycra, so it never was a trademark to lose.

theme: Objects designed by people who were architects by training and profession.
decoy: Iconic furniture and homeware by star designers

members.title: Egg Chair
members.description: Arne Jacobsen's enveloping 1958 swivel lounge chair with a high back.

members.title: Wiggle Side Chair
members.description: Frank Gehry's layered corrugated-cardboard chair from the Easy Edges line.

members.title: Alessi 9093 kettle
members.description: Michael Graves's stovetop kettle with a red bird whistle on the spout.

members.title: La Conica
members.description: Aldo Rossi's conical stovetop espresso pot for Alessi.

members.title: Hill House Chair
members.description: Charles Rennie Mackintosh's tall, black ladder-backed chair of 1902.

members.title: Barrel Chair
members.description: Frank Lloyd Wright's semicircular wooden chair with a vertical-slat back.

members.title: Superleggera
members.description: Gio Ponti's featherweight ash side chair with a woven seat, for Cassina.

members.title: Womb Chair
members.description: Eero Saarinen's fiberglass shell lounge chair made for curling up.

intruders.title: Noguchi Table
intruders.description: Isamu Noguchi's glass top resting on two interlocking wooden supports.
intruders.why: Noguchi was a sculptor, not an architect. His table sits comfortably among mid-century architect-designed classics.

intruders.title: Embryo Chair
intruders.description: Marc Newson's plump neoprene-skinned lounge chair on slim chrome legs.
intruders.why: Newson studied jewelry and sculpture, not architecture.

theme: Seating named for the thing its shape resembles.
decoy: Modern seating with evocative one-word names

members.title: Swan Chair
members.description: Arne Jacobsen's swiveling armchair with curved upswept arms, for a Copenhagen hotel.

members.title: Butterfly Chair
members.description: Leather sling stretched over a looping steel rod, created in Buenos Aires.

members.title: Coconut Chair
members.description: George Nelson's triangular lounge shell on slim steel legs.

members.title: Diamond Chair
members.description: Harry Bertoia's welded steel-wire lounge chair with a padded cover.

members.title: Marshmallow Sofa
members.description: George Nelson's 1956 bench of eighteen round vinyl cushions.

members.title: Tongue Chair
members.description: Pierre Paulin's low stretch-jersey lounger that sits directly on the floor.

members.title: Bubble Chair
members.description: Eero Aarnio's transparent acrylic sphere that sways from a chain.

members.title: Heart Cone Chair
members.description: Verner Panton's upholstered armchair on a cone, with two rounded top lobes.

members.title: Shell Chair
members.description: Hans Wegner's three-legged lounge chair of curved laminated wood.

intruders.title: Louis Ghost
intruders.description: Philippe Starck's clear polycarbonate armchair with an oval Louis XVI back.
intruders.why: Called 'Ghost' for its see-through material; its outline is a Louis XVI armchair, not a ghost.

intruders.title: Djinn Chair
intruders.description: Olivier Mourgue's low foam lounge chair, seen in '2001: A Space Odyssey'.
intruders.why: Named after the spirits of Middle Eastern folklore, not for any resemblance in outline.

theme: Logos that picture the literal meaning of the brand's name.
decoy: Famous pictorial brand logos

members.title: Apple
members.description: Silhouette of a bitten fruit, once striped in rainbow colors.

members.title: Shell
members.description: Red-edged yellow scallop on petrol station canopies.

members.title: Target
members.description: Red bullseye of concentric rings for a Minneapolis retailer.

members.title: Puma
members.description: Leaping big cat in silhouette above a sportswear wordmark.

members.title: Jaguar
members.description: Chrome cat mascot mid-pounce on the hood of British saloons.

members.title: Penguin Books
members.description: Black and white seabird in an orange oval on paperbacks.

members.title: Mitsubishi
members.description: Three red rhombuses meeting at a central point.

members.title: Subaru
members.description: Six silver stars on a blue oval, one larger than the rest.

members.title: Dove
members.description: Gold bird silhouette on bars of moisturizing soap.

intruders.title: Starbucks
intruders.description: Green circle framing a crowned, twin-tailed siren.
intruders.why: The name comes from Starbuck, the first mate in Moby-Dick; the siren has nothing to do with it.

intruders.title: Amazon
intruders.description: Lowercase wordmark underlined by an orange smile-shaped arrow.
intruders.why: Named after the river, but the arrow runs from a to z and shows no river.

intruders.title: Evernote
intruders.description: Green elephant head in profile whose ear is a folded page corner.
intruders.why: The elephant stands for memory; nothing in the name means elephant.

theme: Design icons created by a woman designer.
decoy: Landmark fashion, graphic and furniture icons of the 20th century

members.title: Nike Swoosh
members.description: Curved check-like mark drawn for a running-shoe company in 1971.

members.title: Unikko
members.description: Bold poppy print of big flat blooms for Marimekko, 1964.

members.title: Bibendum Chair
members.description: Plump armchair of stacked tubular rolls on a chrome base, 1920s.

members.title: Wrap dress
members.description: Jersey dress that ties at the waist with no buttons or zips, 1974.

members.title: Chanel 2.55
members.description: Quilted leather handbag with a chain-and-leather shoulder strap, 1955.

members.title: Happy Mac
members.description: Smiling computer face greeting early Macintosh users at startup.

members.title: Calyx
members.description: 1951 abstract furnishing fabric of cup-like motifs on thin stems.

members.title: Citi logo
members.description: Lowercase bank wordmark with a red arc over the t, 1998.

intruders.title: Kelly bag
intruders.description: Trapezoid leather handbag with a flap, strap and padlock, from Hermès.
intruders.why: Designed by Robert Dumas; it only took the name of Grace Kelly, who carried it.

intruders.title: I Love NY logo
intruders.description: Typewriter-style I and NY flanking a red heart, from 1977.
intruders.why: Designed by Milton Glaser. It is as iconic a piece of graphic design as the Swoosh or the Citi arc.

theme: Designs whose form or dimensions are fixed by an ISO or IEC international standard.
decoy: Everyday designs and symbols recognized all over the world

members.title: A4 paper
members.description: Sheet of 210 by 297 mm whose halves keep the same proportions.

members.title: Shipping container
members.description: Corrugated steel box twenty or forty feet long, stacked on cargo ships.

members.title: Payment card
members.description: Plastic card of 85.60 by 53.98 mm with embossed account numbers.

members.title: QR code
members.description: Square grid of black modules with three nested corner squares.

members.title: Radiation trefoil
members.description: Three black blades around a central dot on a yellow field.

members.title: Wheelchair symbol
members.description: White pictogram of a seated wheelchair user on a blue square.

members.title: Running man exit sign
members.description: Green pictogram of a figure hurrying toward a doorway.

members.title: Standby power symbol
members.description: Broken circle pierced by a short vertical line, on device buttons.

members.title: USB-C
members.description: Reversible oval plug for charging and data on phones and laptops.

intruders.title: Lightning connector
intruders.description: Apple's reversible eight-pin plug for charging and data on iPhones.
intruders.why: A proprietary Apple design that no ISO or IEC standard specifies. It was USB-C's direct rival and looks like its twin.

intruders.title: US Letter paper
intruders.description: Sheet of 8.5 by 11 inches used across North America.
intruders.why: Its size comes from American trade practice, later written into ANSI rules, not from ISO 216. It is A4's everyday office counterpart.
